articles.title: In a flap: how the butterfly became a symbol of gen Z resilience – and anxiety
articles.summary: The delicate insect has become fashion’s favourite motif again – but having represented sexuality in the 90s and the soul in Greco-Roman times, what does it say about youth culture today? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: I n the new Gucci campaign, Mariah Carey blows a goodbye kiss to 2026 in the most Mariahhhh way possible. Dressed in a fake fur coat and an azure dress, she enters a Christmas party to the twinkly sounds of All I Want For Christmas Is You. There are beautiful people, presents wrapped with Gucci string and butterflies, which have been associated with the popstar since her 1997 album, Butterfly, but have recently fluttered back to become a symbol of gen Z defiance and girlhood.

Carey serves as fairy godmother to the other “pop girlies” who have embraced the emblem, from PinkPantheress to Dua Lipa; Rachel Chinouriri to Marina and the Diamonds. At the Academy Museum gala in October, the singer Janelle Monáe looked as if she might take flight in a Robert Wun couture gown, with wide, yonic wings. Elsewhere, Tate McRae recently wore a black sequined butterfly bra and matching butterfly wing belt from lingerie wunderkind Ludovic de Saint Sernin. Both Swedish popstar Zara Larsson and her fans are championing glittery butterfly makeup motifs.

articles.title: ‘I was drinking at 15, going to parties, being groomed and abused’: the grim reality of age-gap relationships
articles.summary: Do teenagers need more protection from predatory adults? As campaigners in the UK call for changes to the law on consent, we talk to five people who became entangled with much older men and women.
body: I have spoken to people in their 40s, 50s, 60s and 70s, describing age gaps far greater than three years; often with people twice their age or more. It’s noticeable that social norms and taboos didn’t change hugely between the start of the 1960s and the end of the 80s; in most cases, their parents didn’t bat an eyelid and teachers, if they were aware, didn’t intervene. But the more striking through-line, from the 60s to the 00s, is how these relationships started – almost always through a position of power.

Liz, who is now 56, was an exception to that. When she was in her fifth year at school, she spent a lot of time with her brother, who was six years older. “I was drinking alcohol from the age of 15, going to parties with all these people,” she says. “Being groomed and abused, kind of … well, not kind of. I was groomed and abused, by more than one. This particular chap sticks out. He was by no means the worst person in my life, by the way.”

articles.title: Experience: I discovered my dad was a killer on the run – and turned him in
articles.summary: After a childhood marked by horrifying cruelty, the day finally came when I held my father’s life in the balance. Growing up, I lived in fear of my father’s moods. If there was too much ice in his drink or the sofa cushions weren’t lined up, he’d fly into a rage.
body: My parents managed apartments in the US, so we moved around a lot. I never got to make friends, so I assumed all fathers were the same.

I was eight when we went on a rare family holiday. Dad took me boating and could see I was nervous. “You need to face your fears,” he said, throwing me overboard. When I swam closer, he rowed away. By the time I made it to shore, I was exhausted.

When I was 16, we settled in Michigan. I started dating a girl called Lisa. I was worried about meeting her dad, but he was warm and welcoming. It was a revelation to discover not all men were angry and cruel.

I told Lisa how my father would hold my head under water and made me dangle from balconies. “Chip, that’s not OK,” she told me, horrified. I began to understand how abusive my childhood had been. I moved out, but couldn’t cut off my family completely.
points: After a childhood marked by horrifying cruelty, the day finally came when I held my father’s life in the balance.
Growing up, I lived in fear of my father’s moods.
If there was too much ice in his drink or the sofa cushions weren’t lined up, he’d fly into a rage.
“You need to face your fears,” he said, throwing me overboard.
articles.author: Chip St Clair

articles.title: Pink Rabbit: the provocative bedroom drama about a Muslim OnlyFans star interrupted by her mum
articles.summary: In Farah Ashraf’s solo show an obedient daughter secretly does online sex work as ‘PersianBaby’. The actor and writer explains how two worlds collide in her darkly funny play. At home, Amna is the modest and dutiful Muslim daughter of her parents’ dreams.
body: Pink Rabbit, writer-performer Farah Ashraf’s provocative and darkly funny solo play, is a nuanced account of being caught between the private life of desire and the cultural expectations that shape how she is perceived. “I loved this idea of push and pull, and two different worlds,” says Ashraf who began work on the play during her final year at the Oxford School of Drama, before which she had trained with the National Youth Theatre.

“At the time, I was really struggling and had an inner frustration with how I thought I was going to be perceived when I entered the industry and the roles that I might be limited to playing.” Since graduating, however, Ashraf has appeared in roles across film, TV and stage, including in Netflix’s The Witcher, Riz Ahmed’s series Bait and in a lead role in the coming-of-age play Santi & Naz.

articles.title: The 22 Best European Christmas Markets to Visit This Winter
articles.summary: From Vienna to Helsinki, there’s nothing quite like a Christmas market to offer a mood-boosting hit of festive splendor. Here, find 22 immersive European Christmas markets to make this your merriest holiday season yet.
body: There’s nothing quite like a Christmas market to set a joyful tone for the holiday season. Is there anywhere else where it’s acceptable to mill about with a hearty mug of glögg in one hand, an even larger potato pancake in the other, while exceeding your budget on handcrafted ornaments and posing for photos in front of a wooden sleigh? The answer, we can confidently say, is no.

If you’re especially fortunate, you might even find yourself exploring a traditional European Christmas market this winter—a bucket list item for travelers with a proclivity for all things merry and bright. A natural place to start when curating an itinerary is Germany, and for good reason: It is, after all, the birthplace of the Christmas market, with Dresden’s Striezelmarkt first springing up all the way back in 1434.

But it’s hardly the only country that excels at this holiday event. There are numerous other destinations scattered across the continent—some familiar, and some wonderfully under the radar—that deliver the festive goods. Here, find 22 storybook European Christmas markets to make 2026 your most memorable holiday season yet.
points: From Vienna to Helsinki, there’s nothing quite like a Christmas market to offer a mood-boosting hit of festive splendor.

articles.title: Katie Holmes’s Holiday Party Trick? Matching Her Lipstick to Her Bag
articles.summary: The actor brought a little festive color coordination to her signature understated winter wardrobe, and had boyfriend Jason Bard Yarmosky along too.
body: A flash of red is a holiday party classic, and Katie Holmes is making a persuasive case for doubling down on the festive color. The actor stepped out in New York for a holiday celebration hosted by Meiomi Pinot Noir, with her boyfriend Jason Bard Yarmosky by her side, serving up a masterclass in laidback party dressing.

While fellow guests embraced the season’s faux fur, feathers, and sequins, Holmes stuck to her trusty winter uniform: a sweeping black coat from Lafayette 148 layered over a simple white top and dark Banana Republic corduroys, with black shoes by The Row. The pièce de résistance was a cherry-red Gucci shoulder bag, perfectly coordinated with her punchy red lipstick.

It’s an easy styling trick, but an effective one. The two flashes of crimson brought a festive sensibility to an otherwise pared-back ensemble, while the lipstick also felt particularly appropriate for an evening celebrating Pinot Noir. Holmes looked very much in the holiday spirit, without a sequin in sight.
points: The actor brought a little festive color coordination to her signature understated winter wardrobe, and had boyfriend Jason Bard Yarmosky along too.

articles.title: Sheet-Pan Cider Vinegar Chicken
articles.summary: A one-pan dinner for cozy fall evenings in.
body: Slashing bone-in chicken thighs (carefully, around the bone, of course) allows a punchy maple-Dijon-ACV marinade to permeate the meat deeply in a short amount of time. And that waiting time is well spent: Scatter torn sourdough bread on a baking sheet and bake until crisp, then toss croutons aside to make way for the thighs. Once the chicken is cooked through, toss the croutons in the rendered fat and cook until everything is bronzed and glistening. A few handfuls of arugula make an elegant finish—who needs a side salad?

Whisk 5 garlic cloves, finely grated, ½ cup plus 3 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar, 5 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, 3 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, 1 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. pure maple syrup, 2½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) in a measuring glass or small bowl to combine. Transfer 2 Tbsp. vinegar mixture to a small bowl; set aside.
